blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights AttackTagger, a factor-graph-based framework for preemptive intrusion detection that identifies malicious users before system misuse occurs. The paper's key insight is reasoning about attack stages collectively rather than per-event, leveraging factor graphs to model dependencies between user states, events, and profiles. The author praises the approach for its early detection capabilities (74% of attacks detected before misuse) and its ability to uncover previously unknown malicious users. The use of Gibbs sampling for real-time inference and the simplicity of factor graphs over other graphical models are also noted as noteworthy contributions.
paper_title: Preemptive Intrusion Detection: Theoretical Framework and Real-World Measurements
paper_abstract: This paper presents a Factor Graph based framework called AttackTagger for highly accurate and preemptive detection of attacks, i.e., before the system misuse. We use security logs on real incidents that occurred over a six-year period at the National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA) to evaluate AttackTagger. Our data consist of security incidents that led to compromise of the target system, i.e., the attacks in the incidents were only identified after the fact by security analysts. AttackTagger detected 74 percent of attacks, and the majority them were detected before the system misuse. Finally, AttackTagger uncovered six hidden attacks that were not detected by intrusion detection systems during the incidents or by security analysts in post-incident forensic analysis.
